sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by confocal microscopy (anti-RAET1G co-staining with GFP, L3) and by anti-GFP staining of non-permeabilized HT1080 stable cells (L4). Anti-Myc antibody also accessible at the surface (L4). No NKG2D-binding or NK-cell killing assay was reported for the tagged construct; functional impact NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: The construct architecture described in L2 places GFP and Myc after an exogenous leader peptide and before the RAET1G cDNA, meaning the tag occupies the N-terminus of the mature ectodomain. The authoritative topology landmarks fix the signal-peptide cleavage at residue 25/26; therefore the tag sits at insert_after_residue=25, with residue_before=T (position 25, last SP residue) and residue_after=G (position 26, first mature residue), both read directly from the numbered sequence. No specific residue number is stated in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived: RAET1G has exactly one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus at residue 26), leaving no ambiguity about where the N-terminal tag resides. Surface display was confirmed by two independent methods (L3, L4), supporting high confidence. PMC2637608 (L1–L4): Full-length, membrane-anchored RAET1G1 was expressed from vector PK1 with an exogenous leader peptide followed by GFP, a Myc tag, and a short linker peptide fused to the RAET1G cDNA (L2). The construct was transfected into Cos7 and stably expressed in HT1080 cells. Anti-GFP antibody stained non-permeabilized HT1080 cells at 4°C (L4), and confocal microscopy showed anti-RAET1G antiserum co-localising with GFP signal on the cell surface (L3), confirming the tag is extracellular.

sources.claim: The resulting construct contained a leader peptide followed by GFP, a Myc tag, and a short linker peptide fused to the relevant cDNA.

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) derive from the same publication (PMC2637608) and collectively describe a single N-terminal GFP+Myc tagging event at the mature N-terminus of RAET1G. No internal-loop insertions, C-terminal extracellular tags, or function-abrogating insertions are reported anywhere in the ledger. The intracellular C-terminus (residues 243–334) is not tagged in any ledger line and is therefore not proposed. No other proteins or orthologs are cited in the ledger for RAET1G.
